svg.title: $450,000 Commissions to $157,500 Owner Net
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-03-base-case-commission-waterfall; chart type: waterfall; title: $450,000 Commissions to $157,500 Owner Net; subtitle: Six bars reconcile the canonical Base-Case 35.0% net margin.; chapter number: 3; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Annual USD. Opening revenue and closing owner net are total bars; the four intervening values are negative expense movements. Expense allocations illustrate a reconciliation, not supplied scorecard line items. Contractor fees and deal-variable costs are separate from the recurring operating-overhead budget.; caption: $450,000 − $120,000 − $72,000 − $48,000 − $52,500 = $157,500; $157,500 / $450,000 = 35.0%. Recurring overhead is $4,000 monthly, within the canonical $2,500–$14,000 monthly range; total annual expenses also include variable deal costs. Equipment principal never enters this bridge.; stages: label: Gross broker commissions; value: $450,000 annual revenue from earned broker commissions; numeric value: 450000.0; detail: Opening total: 30 illustrative settlements at $15,000 commission each. Do not add the $7,500,000 underlying equipment value, escrow deposits, or creditor payoffs to this revenue figure.; label: Contractor execution; value: Subtract $120,000 for contracted delivery and transaction support; numeric value: -120000.0; detail: Budget contractor sourcing, coordination, and routine inspection labor across the three-contractor Base pod. Resulting balance: $330,000. Contractor status must follow actual working arrangements rather than the seat label.; label: External deal services; value: Subtract $72,000 for incremental specialist and closing services; numeric value: -72000.0; detail: Budget outside diagnostics, equipment-specific specialist reports, title work, and deal travel borne by the broker. Exclude labor already counted in contractor execution and transport paid directly by buyers. Balance: $258,000.; label: Recurring operating overhead; value: Subtract $48,000 for twelve months of operating infrastructure; numeric value: -48000.0; detail: Allocate $4,000 monthly to CRM, inventory matching, buyer alerts, insurance, bookkeeping, and communications. This is the recurring overhead component, not the total monthly equivalent of every expense. Balance: $210,000.; label: Acquisition and settlement friction; value: Subtract $52,500 for acquisition, settlement fees, and losses; numeric value: -52500.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $30,000 to buyer and seller acquisition, $12,000 to broker-borne settlement charges, and $10,500 to realized claim or collection losses. Count each expense once. Resulting balance: $157,500.; label: Annual owner net profit; value: $157,500 owner net equals thirty-five percent of revenue; numeric value: 157500.0; detail: Closing total, not an additional upward movement. Preserve the canonical owner-net definition: no extra owner salary or personal tax adjustment is introduced. Conservative remains $100,000 × 25% = $25,000; Scaled remains $800,000 × 45% = $360,000.

circle.title: label: Gross broker commissions; value: $450,000 annual revenue from earned broker commissions; numeric value: 450000.0; detail: Opening total: 30 illustrative settlements at $15,000 commission each. Do not add the $7,500,000 underlying equipment value, escrow deposits, or creditor payoffs to this revenue figure.

label: Contractor execution; value: Subtract $120,000 for contracted delivery and transaction support; numeric value: -120000.0; detail: Budget contractor sourcing, coordination, and routine inspection labor across the three-contractor Base pod. Resulting balance: $330,000. Contractor status must follow actual working arrangements rather than the seat label.

label: External deal services; value: Subtract $72,000 for incremental specialist and closing services; numeric value: -72000.0; detail: Budget outside diagnostics, equipment-specific specialist reports, title work, and deal travel borne by the broker. Exclude labor already counted in contractor execution and transport paid directly by buyers. Balance: $258,000.

label: Recurring operating overhead; value: Subtract $48,000 for twelve months of operating infrastructure; numeric value: -48000.0; detail: Allocate $4,000 monthly to CRM, inventory matching, buyer alerts, insurance, bookkeeping, and communications. This is the recurring overhead component, not the total monthly equivalent of every expense. Balance: $210,000.

label: Acquisition and settlement friction; value: Subtract $52,500 for acquisition, settlement fees, and losses; numeric value: -52500.0; detail: Illustratively allocate $30,000 to buyer and seller acquisition, $12,000 to broker-borne settlement charges, and $10,500 to realized claim or collection losses. Count each expense once. Resulting balance: $157,500.

label: Annual owner net profit; value: $157,500 owner net equals thirty-five percent of revenue; numeric value: 157500.0; detail: Closing total, not an additional upward movement. Preserve the canonical owner-net definition: no extra owner salary or personal tax adjustment is introduced. Conservative remains $100,000 × 25% = $25,000; Scaled remains $800,000 × 45% = $360,000.
